sheets.title: What is a force, really?
sheets.question: The first law is recited as "a body keeps moving unless pushed". Why is it a definition of the frame rather than a law about forces?
sheets.takeaway: pick the frame first: a force is what an inertial frame says it is

sheets.title: Is F = ma the law, or a special case?
sheets.question: Rockets, falling chains and conveyor belts all have mass entering or leaving. Which form of Newton's second law survives all three?
sheets.takeaway: F = dp/dt is the law; F = ma is the fixed-mass shorthand

sheets.title: Why is the normal force not the reaction to weight?
sheets.question: Equal and opposite sounds like a pair. What extra conditions turn two forces into a third-law pair?
sheets.takeaway: a pair needs two bodies and one interaction; N and mg are neither

sheets.title: How do you draw a diagram that never lies?
sheets.question: Six forces, one acceleration. What procedure makes the equations fall out in one pass?
sheets.takeaway: isolate one body, name every agent, put the axes along the acceleration

sheets.title: What does a weighing scale actually measure?
sheets.question: In a lift the scale reads more, less, or nothing at all. Which force is it reporting?
sheets.takeaway: weight never changes; the reading is the normal force

sheets.title: Three forces, no acceleration: why does the triangle close?
sheets.question: A lamp hangs on two wires. When is the sine rule faster than resolving components?
sheets.takeaway: three forces in equilibrium close a triangle, and the sine rule reads it

sheets.title: Is friction equal to mu N?
sheets.question: A 20 N block sits on a rough floor while you push with 3 N and it does not move. What is the friction force?
sheets.takeaway: static friction is an inequality with a ceiling, not a number

sheets.title: Which way does friction point?
sheets.question: A block is dropped on a moving belt and another slides up a ramp. Both are moving, yet friction points in opposite senses. Why?
sheets.takeaway: friction opposes relative slip at the contact, not motion in the room

sheets.title: Why is the easiest pull not horizontal?
sheets.question: Dragging a crate is easier with the rope tilted up. Why, and exactly how much less force is needed?
sheets.takeaway: tilting up trades normal force for drive, and the best tilt is arctan mu

sheets.title: When do two stacked blocks stop moving together?
sheets.question: You push the lower block of a stack. What limits how hard you can push before the top one slips?
sheets.takeaway: the top block is driven by friction alone, so it caps the whole system

sheets.title: System or single body: which do you solve?
sheets.question: Two blocks are pushed together. How do you get both the common acceleration and the force between them, without solving twice?
sheets.takeaway: use the system for the acceleration, then isolate one body for the internal force

sheets.title: Atwood on a ramp: where does the motion change hands?
sheets.question: One mass hangs, one sits on a rough 30° ramp. Over what range of mass ratio does nothing move at all?
sheets.takeaway: friction turns one crossing point into a band of mass ratios

sheets.title: Why does the free end move twice as far?
sheets.question: A rope runs over a fixed pulley, round a movable one, and is anchored. What links the accelerations, and what links the tensions?
sheets.takeaway: the length constraint gives the accelerations; one string gives the tension

sheets.title: Should you ever add a force that is not there?
sheets.question: In a braking bus a hanging pendulum swings forward. Add a pseudo force, or stay in the ground frame?
sheets.takeaway: a pseudo force is frame bookkeeping, not an interaction

sheets.title: Is centripetal force a new force?
sheets.question: A ball on a string, a car on a bank, a car over a crest. Which real force points inward in each case?
sheets.takeaway: centripetal force is the inward resultant, never an extra arrow

sheets.title: Why are racetrack corners banked?
sheets.question: With no friction at all, is there still a speed at which a car can take a banked curve?
sheets.takeaway: a bank turns normal force into centripetal force without any friction

sheets.title: How much slower or faster can you take the bank?
sheets.question: Friction turns one design speed into a range. What are the two limits, and what sets them?
sheets.takeaway: friction widens a single design speed into a band of allowed speeds

sheets.title: Why does a conical pendulum ignore the mass?
sheets.question: A bob whirled on a string traces a horizontal circle. What actually sets the period?
sheets.takeaway: the vertical component carries the weight, so only L cos theta enters the period

sheets.title: What is the slowest a ball can go round a vertical loop?
sheets.question: A ball on a string is whirled in a vertical circle. Why must it be fast at the bottom, and what happens at the top?
sheets.takeaway: the string can only pull, so at the top it must still be taut

sheets.title: Why can a bead on a rod stop at the top?
sheets.question: A bead threaded on a light rod is given just enough speed to reach the highest point. What is different from the string?
sheets.takeaway: a rod pushes as well as pulls, so it needs no minimum speed at the top

sheets.title: Why is energy faster than forces in a vertical circle?
sheets.question: The tangential equation has a sin theta in it and the radial equation has a v squared. How do you avoid integrating at all?
sheets.takeaway: energy gives the speed at every angle; the radial equation gives the tension

sheets.title: What changes when the table is rough?
sheets.question: A block on a rough table is tied over a pulley to a hanging mass. Everything is the same as the smooth case except one term. Which one?
sheets.takeaway: on the table friction is the brake; on the string it is the drive

sheets.title: Can an accelerating ramp hold a block still?
sheets.question: A block sits on a frictionless ramp that is itself accelerating horizontally. Is there a ramp acceleration at which the block does not slide at all?
sheets.takeaway: accelerate the ramp at g tan theta and the pseudo force replaces gravity along the face

sheets.title: How do you measure friction without a force meter?
sheets.question: Friction coefficients are quoted to two digits. Which three independent experiments produce them, and what does each one assume?
sheets.takeaway: three routes to one number: tilt, brake, and drag at constant speed

sheets.title: Why does a chain accelerate faster as it falls?
sheets.question: A chain hangs over a table edge with length l already off. The driving weight grows as more falls, but the mass being accelerated does not. What motion results?
sheets.takeaway: the hanging weight grows while the sliding mass stays the same, so a grows with x

sheets.title: How hard must you push a wedge to carry its block?
sheets.question: A block rests on a smooth wedge. Accelerate the wedge horizontally and the block can stay put. What is the required acceleration, and what keeps it there?
sheets.takeaway: at a0 = g tan theta the pseudo force exactly replaces the downhill pull

sheets.title: Is there friction on a block tied to the axis?
sheets.question: A block on a turntable is tied by a string to the centre and the table spins fast. Is the friction zero, or maximum?
sheets.takeaway: the string and friction share one job, so each takes only what it must

sheets.title: Why does a coin and a brick slip at the same speed?
sheets.question: Two objects of very different mass sit at the same radius on a spinning turntable. Which one slides off first?
sheets.takeaway: the friction limit is proportional to mass, so mass cancels out of the slip condition

sheets.title: Why is the block's acceleration not along the face?
sheets.question: A wedge slides on a table and a block slides down its face. You know both motions are linked, but how?
sheets.takeaway: a contact is a coordinate constraint first and a force second

sheets.title: What is g inside a lift, a car, a centrifuge?
sheets.question: A pendulum in an accelerating vehicle keeps time differently. How much, and in which direction does it hang?
sheets.takeaway: g_eff is the vector sum of gravity and the frame acceleration, taken with a minus sign

sheets.title: When does a block leave a wedge that is pulled away?
sheets.question: The wedge is yanked horizontally out from under a block resting on its face. At what acceleration does contact break?
sheets.takeaway: contact survives only while the normal force remains positive

sheets.title: Why can you ignore the normal force in a work calculation?
sheets.question: A constraint force can be large, yet contributes nothing to the energy bookkeeping. Why exactly?
sheets.takeaway: a constraint force perpendicular to the allowed displacement does no work

sheets.title: At what length does a rope over an edge start to slide?
sheets.question: A rope lies on a rough table with length x hanging over the edge. How much must hang before it moves?
sheets.takeaway: the hanging fraction must beat friction on the part still on the table

sheets.title: Does a falling chain weigh three times as much?
sheets.question: A chain is dropped so that it lands in a heap on a scale. At the instant the last link lands, what does the scale read?
sheets.takeaway: a landing chain must be stopped as well as held: three times the landed weight

sheets.title: Why is the cost of speed logarithmic?
sheets.question: A rocket reaches 9 km/s with an exhaust speed of 3 km/s. Why must it be mostly fuel, and how much?
sheets.takeaway: each unit of speed costs a fixed ratio of mass, so speed grows as a logarithm

sheets.title: Why does a conveyor belt need twice the power?
sheets.question: Sand falls vertically onto a belt moving at constant speed. The belt's motor supplies power. Where does it go?
sheets.takeaway: half the power becomes kinetic energy, half is lost to friction while the sand slips

sheets.title: Why does lifting a chain cost more than its weight?
sheets.question: A chain is pulled up from a heap at constant speed. The force is larger than the weight of the hanging part. By how much?
sheets.takeaway: lifting at constant speed still costs a momentum-flux force, lambda v squared

sheets.title: Why can one hand hold a ship?
sheets.question: A rope takes two turns round a bollard and a small force holds a huge one. What is the law, and where does the ratio come from?
sheets.takeaway: every radian of wrap multiplies the grip by e to the mu theta

sheets.title: How does a friction hitch hold a falling climber?
sheets.question: A rope wrapped round a carabiner holds with a small hand force. How many turns does it take to turn 1 into 10, and into 300?
sheets.takeaway: the hitch holds because tension decays exponentially along the wrap

sheets.title: Why does staging beat one big tank?
sheets.question: Two rockets carry the same fuel and the same structure, but one drops an empty stage. How much speed does that buy?
sheets.takeaway: staging wins by throwing away dead structure before the next burn

sheets.title: When is it safe to ignore gravity during a hit?
sheets.question: A bat hits a ball for about a millisecond. Gravity never switches off — so why does every solution drop it?
sheets.takeaway: a force that is huge for a millisecond makes gravity irrelevant

sheets.title: Why does a spinning hoop push its bead up the wire?
sheets.question: A bead slides on a hoop spinning about its vertical diameter. Below a critical spin it sits at the bottom. What happens above it?
sheets.takeaway: above the critical spin the bottom becomes unstable and two new seats appear

sheets.title: At what angle does a slackening string let go?
sheets.question: Launch a ball round a vertical circle too slowly and the string goes limp before the top. Is the release angle predictable?
sheets.takeaway: the slack angle is where the tension reaches zero while the radial equation still holds

sheets.title: How far does a bouncing ball travel before it stops?
sheets.question: A ball is dropped from height h and returns to e squared times that height after each bounce. The bounces are infinite — is the total distance?
sheets.takeaway: an infinite number of bounces still sums to a finite distance and a finite time

sheets.title: Is horizontal momentum really conserved on a wedge?
sheets.question: A block slides down a smooth wedge that is free to move on a smooth table. Which quantity is conserved, and how do you check it in one line?
sheets.takeaway: no external horizontal force means the recoil is the block horizontal momentum, reversed

sheets.title: Where should the fuel go between two stages?
sheets.question: Two stages, 800 kg of fuel, 50 kg of dry structure each. Put 400 kg in each, or 160 in the first and 640 in the second?
sheets.takeaway: with fixed dry masses the split has no interior optimum: fuel early is never worth it

sheets.title: Where exactly do Newton’s laws stop being true?
sheets.question: Newtonian mechanics is taught as if it were exact. Under what conditions does it fail, and what replaces it?
sheets.takeaway: Newton is exact inside a fence, and knowing the fence is what makes the model honest

sheets.title: If a rolling wheel is not sliding, what is friction doing?
sheets.question: A driven wheel has friction at the contact, yet the contact point does not move. How can a force act at a point at rest?
sheets.takeaway: a rolling wheel uses static friction; the contact point is instantaneously at rest

sheets.title: What are the four moves that solve almost every problem here?
sheets.question: The chapter has fourteen sections and one page of results. Which four procedures actually carry the load?
sheets.takeaway: four shortcuts, one theme: replace a hard dynamics question with a smaller one

sheets.title: Can a monkey climb away from its own counterweight?
sheets.question: A monkey and an equal counterweight hang from one rope over a pulley. The monkey climbs. Does the counterweight stay, rise, or fall?
sheets.takeaway: equal masses on one rope share one acceleration: the climb rate drops out entirely
